rationale:
Evidence from iteration 2 (widened sensors at x = ±0.030 m with 16 mm footprints, kp 6.0, kd 0.3, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05, last_direction): all 60 trials still went off track, but line losses fell from 2 to 1 per run. Progress is 0.31 (oval), 0.16 (s-bend) and 0.11 (slalom). max_error is 0.061 to 0.063, just over the 0.06 off-track limit, and steering_oscillation is 0.14 to 0.17, which is low. So the failure is still the robot drifting past the edge at the first large offset, not jitter. Body width cannot relax the limit (it stays at 0.06 for body_width up to 0.18), so the fix must come from control.

Changes: (1) kp 6.0 to 7.0. Feedback (d) allows this when oscillation stays low, and 0.14 to 0.17 is well below the 0.2 threshold. A stronger response at the edge should keep max_error under 0.06. (2) kd 0.3 to 0.4. The higher kp raises effective gain, so a little more damping limits any rise in oscillation. (3) Keep geometry, base_speed 1.4, ki 0.05 and last_direction. This isolates the gain change. Speed was lowered earlier and helped progress, and the single remaining line loss does not yet point to a different line_loss mode.

Expected result: max_error below 0.06, line_loss_events at 1 or lower, steering_oscillation at or below about 0.2, and progress increasing on all tracks. Risks: kp 7 may oscillate on the slalom. If oscillation exceeds 0.2, next raise kd to 0.5 before cutting kp. If max_error stays above 0.06 with low oscillation, next test a wider array (±0.040 m) with kp near 8. If progress stalls below 1 while max_error stays under 0.06, raise base_speed toward 1.6. Measurements requested: max_error, line_loss_events, progress and steering_oscillation per track, plus rms_error and completion_time.
